vetSays.line: A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm walks away from Haven. They don't look back.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
You catch fragments by the fire — A person, maybe 60s, with tattooed arms telling A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm about you. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.

🔥 The fire settles. the woman in her 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm, the professor has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "The creek went still, and your arm-hairs stood up — I put it down today." "The water goes glass-still. A faint crackling, and the hairs on your arms lift." "The crackling fades. It slides backward into the black water, done spending itself — for now." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Ekai says quietly "Tell me you didn't go alone." A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Greta is showing everyone colonies of umbrella-like leaves, single lemon-sized fruit hidden underneath by the fire. "See the leaves? Like that. Don't mix it up." The journal grows — the human way.
